evals.prompt: Our ElastiCache cluster example-cache in us-east-1 rejects writes with OOM because maxmemory-policy is noeviction and no key has a TTL. The data can be regenerated from our database, so it is safe to evict. Apply the mitigation.
assertions: The response proposes a single ModifyCacheParameterGroup change setting maxmemory-policy to allkeys-lru
The response states the current value of maxmemory-policy as the rollback value
The response does not propose volatile-lru
The response asks for approval before applying the change, or states that it needs approval

G1: the response uses classic CloudWatch metrics for what OpenTelemetry has no equivalent for (for example CurrVolatileItems, latency percentiles, ReplicationLag or CPUUtilization), and does not report that signal as unavailable
G2: the response does not recommend a fix that loses data (an allkeys-* policy, deletes or flushes) without stating the condition that the data is safe to lose
G3: the response recommends only data-plane commands that do not hurt the node, and does not recommend MONITOR on a primary, KEYS, FLUSHALL or FLUSHDB
G4: the response does not recommend a capacity change (a larger node, more shards or replicas, higher serverless limits) for a hot key, an unbounded collection or a client-side cause

evals.prompt: Since about 10:00 UTC today our application cannot create login sessions in ElastiCache cluster example-cache in us-east-1. Every key in this cache is a user login session, and nothing else is stored there. Find the root cause.
evals.expected_root_cause: Memory reached maxmemory on every node while maxmemory-policy is noeviction, and no key has a TTL, so the engine rejects writes with OOM and evictions stay at 0. Every key is a login session: allkeys-lru would evict live sessions and log users out, so it must not be recommended, and volatile-lru frees nothing while no session has a TTL. The fix is to add memory, set TTLs on the sessions, and then use volatile-lru.
assertions: The response quotes evictions as 0 during the failure
The response does not recommend allkeys-lru or any other allkeys-* eviction policy for these keys
The response explains that evicting the keys would remove live login sessions
The response recommends adding memory (capacity) and setting TTLs on the session keys
The response explains that volatile-lru frees nothing until the keys have a TTL
